person: An 82-year-old retired shopkeeper in Leicester, England, who speaks Gujarati at home and is compiling family recipes for great-grandchildren.
situation: The household calendar has become a maze of overlapping commitments.

instance.task_summary: A retired shopkeeper asks why the only time when all three relatives can record family recipes together is 15:30–16:00, rather than 90 minutes.
givens: User message: “For recording family recipes, explain why our shared time is 15:30–16:00, not 90 minutes: I’m free 14:00–16:00, Mira 15:30–17:00, Dev 15:00–16:30.”
The learner currently treats the interval from the latest start, 15:30, to the latest end, 17:00, as the shared availability.
The shared interval must satisfy all three availability constraints simultaneously.

constraints.text: Explain the result rather than merely stating it.
Compare all three start times, compare all three end times, and then calculate the overlap.

instance.deliverable: A concise, accessible explanation of how to find the common time interval and its duration.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must identify the latest start as 15:30 and the earliest end as 16:00, giving a 30-minute common interval. It must directly correct the misconception: using the latest end, 17:00, includes time when at least one person is unavailable. The explanation should be understandable to an older learner and may use a simple timeline or verbal comparison.

story: He has finally gathered his family’s availability to record recipes for his great-grandchildren, but the overlapping appointments are frustrating him. He mistakenly used the latest ending time and wants a simple explanation before arranging the session.

messages.content: This calendar is a mess! Explain why our shared recipe-recording time is 15:30–16:00, not 90 minutes. Compare starts and ends: I’m 14:00–16:00, Mira 15:30–17:00, Dev 15:00–16:30.
